Container.Name: Euro-Office
Container.Overview:
Euro Office Document Server - a sovereign, European document server for browser-based editing of text documents, spreadsheets and presentations. It is a maintained fork of the OnlyOffice Document Server, so it speaks the same WOPI and OnlyOffice APIs and plugs straight into OpenCloud (and Nextcloud/ownCloud). Use it to edit .docx / .xlsx / .pptx and .odt / .ods / .odp files right in your browser, without any desktop office suite.
This is a thin wrapper (github.com/junkerderprovinz/euro-office) around the official image. It fixes an upstream permission bug on the Data folder, serves https out of the box with a certificate it creates for itself, and replaces the vendor's start page with one that shows what to enter in OpenCloud.
This is not a standalone app. It is the editor behind a file server: you point your cloud (e.g. the OpenCloud container) at it and edit the files stored in that cloud. On its own it only shows its start page.
How it fits together (with OpenCloud): • Install this container. Set a JWT secret below and remember it. • Click the WebUI button. The browser warns about the certificate once, because Euro Office made it for itself; accept the warning. The page that opens says whether the editor is ready and lists the three OpenCloud fields. • In the OpenCloud template set "Web office suite" = euro-office, "Office document server URL" = https://[THIS-SERVER-IP]:9943 and "Office WOPI secret" = the same value as the JWT secret here. • The New button in OpenCloud now offers documents, spreadsheets and presentations, and existing Office files open in Euro Office. • Every other browser or device you edit documents on has to accept the certificate once as well, by opening https://[THIS-SERVER-IP]:9943. With your own trusted certificate (see "Own certificate" below) that step goes away.
First start: • The document server bundles its own database and converter and takes a minute or two to come up on the very first start. Its start page says when it is ready. • Leave the "Database" and "Logs" fields under Advanced View blank. Neither is required, and mounting a fresh empty folder over either one hides a directory the image ships pre-built, which stops the container from starting (see Troubleshooting below).
Security / reverse proxy: • Keep "Enable JWT" = true (the default). The JWT secret signs every request between your cloud and the editor, so never leave it blank. • Behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS (e.g. https://office.example.com), point the proxy at the plain http port (9900) and use the proxy's https URL in OpenCloud. • "Allow self-signed upstream" is true by default because OpenCloud on Unraid serves a self-signed certificate. Set it to false only when your cloud has a valid certificate.
Own certificate: • Put the certificate and its private key into the Certificates folder (default /mnt/user/appdata/euro-office/certs), then set "TLS certificate" = /certs/cert.pem and "TLS private key" = /certs/key.pem under Advanced View. Unraid's combined *_unraid_bundle.pem works too: copy it in and enter that one file in both fields. The key must not be passphrase-protected. • After Apply the container log shows "SSL enabled with cert=/certs/...". If it still names /var/www/euro-office/Data/certs, one of the two paths is wrong and Euro Office fell back to its own certificate.
Troubleshooting - container loops "PostgreSQL ... is not accessible or does not exist": • Your "Database" field under Advanced View has a path in it. Open the container's Edit page, switch on Advanced View, clear the "Database" field completely, then Apply. The bundled, already-initialised database takes over and the container starts normally within a minute.
Troubleshooting - container loops "Starting nginx nginx ...fail!": • Your "Logs" field under Advanced View has a path in it. The image keeps its log tree at /var/log/euro-office/documentserver, so mounting an empty folder over /var/log/euro-office hides it, nginx cannot open its error log there, and the entrypoint aborts before the editor comes up. Open the container's Edit page, switch on Advanced View, clear the "Logs" field completely, then Apply. • The logs are not lost by clearing the field - the Unraid log button on the container still shows everything the server prints.
Troubleshooting - documents open blank, or the browser says "this content is blocked, contact the site owner": • OpenCloud's "Office document server URL" still starts with http://. A browser refuses to load an http editor inside the https OpenCloud page, and since the request is never sent, neither container logs anything. Change it to https://[THIS-SERVER-IP]:9943; the OpenCloud log warns about this at startup. • Or this browser has not accepted the certificate yet: open https://[THIS-SERVER-IP]:9943 and accept the warning. • Or the "HTTPS Port" mapping is missing on an older install: add a port with container port 443 and host port 9943 on the Edit page.
About Euro Office: • Euro Office is an open, sovereignty-focused document server developed in Europe as an OnlyOffice-compatible fork. Because it is API-compatible, any guide for "OnlyOffice Document Server + OpenCloud/Nextcloud" applies here as well.
Project: https://github.com/euro-office/documentserver This is an independent, community-maintained Unraid packaging and is not affiliated with the Euro Office project.

Config.Name: HTTPS Port
Config.Description: The editor's https port. In OpenCloud, set 'Office document server URL' to https://[THIS-SERVER-IP]:9943. Euro Office creates its own certificate on the first start, so open that address once in your browser and accept the warning.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Plain http port. OpenCloud runs on https, and browsers will not show an http editor inside it, so use the HTTPS Port for OpenCloud. This one is for a reverse proxy that terminates TLS itself.

Config.Name: JWT secret
Config.Description: Shared secret that signs every request between your cloud and this editor. REQUIRED. Pick a long random string. It MUST be identical to the 'Office WOPI secret' you set in the OpenCloud template. Keep it secret.

Config.Name: Enable WOPI
Config.Description: Turns on the WOPI protocol that OpenCloud uses to open and save documents. Keep 'true' - with 'false' OpenCloud cannot use this editor.

Config.Name: Enable JWT
Config.Description: Require the signed JWT on every request. Keep 'true' for security. Only set 'false' for isolated testing on a trusted LAN.

Config.Name: Allow self-signed upstream
Config.Description: Lets the editor fetch and save documents from a cloud with a self-signed certificate, which is what OpenCloud on Unraid serves by default. Set 'false' only when your cloud has a valid certificate.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Optional. Persistent document-server data (keys, fonts cache, forgotten files). Recommended for a permanent install; can be omitted for a purely stateless WOPI backend.

Config.Name: Logs
Config.Description: Leave BLANK for a normal install. The image builds its log tree at /var/log/euro-office/documentserver (nginx.error.log plus one folder per service). Mounting an EMPTY folder over /var/log/euro-office hides that tree, nginx then cannot open its error log and fails with 'Starting nginx nginx ...fail!', and because the entrypoint stops on that error the container crash-loops on every boot. You lose nothing by leaving this blank: the Unraid log button still shows everything the server prints. Only set a path here if it already contains the log tree copied out of a running container first.

Config.Name: Database
Config.Description: Leave BLANK for a normal install. The image ships with an already-initialised database baked in; mounting an EMPTY folder here hides that database and the container fails to start with 'PostgreSQL ... is not accessible or does not exist' on every boot (an upstream bug: the entrypoint cannot initialise a database in a fresh empty volume - see euro-office/documentserver#299). Without this mount the DB simply resets on container recreate, which is fine for WOPI use with OpenCloud. Only set a path here if it already contains a working euro-office Postgres data directory copied out of a running container first.

Config.Name: Certificates
Config.Description: Optional. Folder for your own TLS certificate and private key, used by the two fields below. Drop cert.pem and key.pem into /mnt/user/appdata/euro-office/certs on the server, then set the fields to /certs/cert.pem and /certs/key.pem. An empty folder here changes nothing.

Config.Name: TLS certificate
Config.Description: Leave blank to use the certificate Euro Office creates for itself. For your own, enter its path inside the container, e.g. /certs/cert.pem (not the /mnt/user/... path). Unraid's combined *_unraid_bundle.pem holds certificate and key in one file: enter that same file here and in 'TLS private key'. If either path is wrong, Euro Office falls back to its own certificate and says so in the log.

Config.Name: TLS private key
Config.Description: Leave blank to use the certificate Euro Office creates for itself. Otherwise the path inside the container to the key that belongs to 'TLS certificate', e.g. /certs/key.pem. The key must not be passphrase-protected (create it with openssl's -nodes option).

Config.Name: Send HSTS header
Config.Description: 'true' (the default) tells browsers to use https for this host for a year. It only matters with your own trusted certificate and a hostname: browsers ignore it for IP addresses and for the self-signed certificate. Set 'false' if that hostname also serves things you reach over plain http, e.g. unraid.example.com, because the rule applies to the whole hostname regardless of port.
